newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says no mediation to end rebel war.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says no mediation to end rebel war.

text.p: Sri Lanka on Monday played down a reported secret visit by a Tamil Tiger rebel leader from France and said there was no possibility of the 13-year-old ethnic strife being resolved through mediation.

Sri Lankan newspapers reported on Sunday that Lawrence Thilakar, the Paris-based international spokesman for the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), had secretly arrived in northern Sri Lanka to try to broker a deal to end the Indian Ocean island's long ethnic war.
The newspapers said Thilakar had come to brief LTTE chief Velupillai Prabhakaran on possible moves to resume peace talks.
But government officials denied any moves for mediation.
"The question of mediation is not on the cards at this point," a government spokesman told Reuters.

Diplomatic sources confirmed Thilakar's presence in northern Sri Lanka, but said it was unlikely the government would accept mediation by a third party to help end the war as it had rejected such offers in the past.
The LTTE is fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east.
Sri Lankan Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar told Reuters in an interview last month that the conflict was an internal matter that had to be resolved by the government and the LTTE.
"It (mediation) becomes an interference in our internal affairs and we will not tolerate it at all," Kadirgamar said.

Newspapers said Thilakar had entered the country via Nepal and India using a false name. They said he had arrived on a rebel-owned cargo ship and been picked up by rebel boats off the northwestern Mannar area.
They said Thilakar had held talks with Western political leaders who had pledged their support for fresh peace talks, but did not give details.
Sri Lankan President Chandrika Kumaratunga recently said she was confident of finishing the war by the year's end because of a series of successful military campaigns against the rebels.
Last week the army said at least 200 rebels and 65 soldiers were killed when the LTTE attacked the Vaunathivu army camp in Batticaloa, some 200 km (125 miles) from capital Colombo.
The Tigers said only 84 rebels were killed.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died since the civil war began in 1983.
